Surah al-Shams (The Sun)

Makki; its verses are fifteen.

﴿By the sun and its brightness.﴾ That is: its light when it rises and its dominion is established. It is said: al-ḍaḥwa (the forenoon) is the rising of the day, and al-ḍuḥā (the morning brightness) is beyond that, while al-ḍuḥā with a fatḥa and a long vowel (ḍaḥāʾ) is when the day has extended and is nearly at its midpoint.

"By the moon when it follows it" (﴿وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلَاهَا﴾): that is, when it rises after the sun has set. It was also said: when its rising follows the sun's rising. And it was said: when it follows the sun in roundness and full brightness.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 91, verse 3:

﴿By the day when it reveals it,﴾ i.e., when it reveals the sun, for it becomes manifest (tajalla) when the day spreads out. So it is as if the day revealed it, even though it is the sun that spreads the day. Or [it means] it reveals the darkness, or the world, or the earth, even though no mention of them has preceded, because they are known.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 91, verse 4:

﴿By the night when it covers it.﴾ That is: [it covers] the sun, so that it veils its light; or [it covers] the horizons; or [it covers] the earth. And since the conjunctive waws (al-wawat al-'atifah) are substitutes for the first waw of oath (al-waw al-qasamiyyah), which stands in the place of the verb, and the ba' (the preposition of oath) serves in place of both of them together, as in your saying: "uqsimu billah" (I swear by God), they deserve to act both as the verb and as the preposition together, just as you say: "Darab Zayd 'Amran, wa Bakrun wa Khalidan" (Zayd struck 'Amr, and Bakr [struck] and Khalid).

﴿And the heaven and what built it﴾. That is, *and He who built it*. The choice of *ما* (*ma*) over *مَن* (*man*) is to express the attributive sense (*al-wasfiyyah*, the sense of a quality or description) for the sake of magnification, as if it had been said: "and by the Mighty One of great majesty who built it." Taking *ما* as a verbal-noun particle (*masdariyyah*, meaning "the verbal noun of") would disrupt the noble composition (*al-nazm al-karim*).
The same applies to His words, exalted is He: ﴿And the earth and He who spread it out﴾ (i.e., He spread it out on every side, just as in "daḥāhā").

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 91, verse 7:

(p-164) ﴿And a soul and He who proportioned it﴾. That is: He brought it into being and originated it, prepared for its perfection. The indefiniteness of "soul" (nafs) is for magnification, on the basis that the intended soul is the soul of Adam, peace be upon him; or it is for multiplicity, and this is more suitable to the answer (to the oath).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 91, verse 8:

﴿So He inspired it with its wickedness and its piety.﴾ That is: He made it understand both of them, and made known to it their states of goodness and ugliness and what each of them leads to, and enabled it to choose whichever of the two it wished. The mention of wickedness first is for the sake of observing the fawasil (the rhyming endings of verses).

"Surely he has succeeded who purifies it." (﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ مَن زَكّاها﴾) That is: he attains every desired goal and is saved from every disliked thing, [he who] causes it to grow and exalts it through piety. It is the answer to the oath, and the lam (of emphasis) has been omitted because of the length of the speech.

The repetition of "qad" in His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿And he has indeed failed who suppresses it﴾, serves to highlight the utmost concern with establishing the truth of its content, and to signal that the oath is also directly connected to it. That is, "He has lost who diminished it and concealed it through immorality." The root of دسى (dassa) is دَسَّسَ (dassasa), like تَقَضّى (taqadda) and تَقَضَّضَ (taqaddaḍa). It has been said that this is a statement following His statement, ﴿So He inspired it with its immorality and its piety﴾, by way of digression (istitrad). The actual answer (jawab) to the oath is what has been omitted, relying on the indication of His statement: *

﴿Thamud denied (their prophet) in their rebelliousness.﴾ The sense is as if it were said: Allah, exalted is He, will surely destroy the disbelievers of Makkah for their denial of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), just as He destroyed Thamud for their denial of Salih, peace be upon him. On the first reading, this is a resumptive sentence (istinaf) that comes to confirm the meaning of His words: ﴿And he has failed who corrupts it.﴾ The word *tughwa*, with a fatha on the *ta'*, means transgression (*tughyan*). The *ba'* (in *bi-tughwaha*) is causal, meaning: they committed denial because of their transgression, just as one says, "He wronged me with his audacity toward Allah, exalted is He." Or it is connected to the denial, meaning: they denied what they were threatened with of the punishment that brings transgression, as in His words: ﴿So they were destroyed by the overwhelming (blast).﴾ It has also been read as *bi-tughwaha* with a damma on the *ta'*, which is likewise a verbal noun (*masdar*), like *ruj'a* (as in ﴿Indeed, to your Lord is the return (*al-ruj'a*).﴾).

Verse 12: ﴿When the most wretched of them broke forth﴾ is in the accusative, governed either by "kadhdhabat" (they denied) or by "al-taghwa" (the transgression). That is, [it refers to] the time when the most wretched of Thamud arose, namely Qidar ibn Salif, or [it refers to] him and those who took upon themselves, along with him, the slaughtering of the she-camel from among the wretched ones. For the elative form (af'al al-tafdil), when it is put in the genitive construction (idafa), is suitable for the singular and the plural, the masculine and the feminine. The excess of their wretchedness over all others lies in their direct undertaking of the slaughter, together with all of them sharing in approval of it.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 91, verse 13:

﴿Then the Messenger of Allah said to them﴾ i.e., to Thamud, ﴿the Messenger of Allah﴾, i.e., Salih, upon him be peace. He referred to him by the title of messengerhood, to announce the obligation of obeying him and to show the extent of their insolence and their persistence in transgression. This is the secret behind the attribution of the she-camel to Allah the Exalted in His saying, ﴿the she-camel of Allah﴾ (p-165).

That is: leave the she-camel of Allah, ﴿and her drink﴾, and do not drive her away from it during her turn.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 91, verse 14:

﴿So they denied him⦆ That is, in his warning, by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you the punishment of a painful day.﴾ It has also been permitted that the pronoun refers to them, the two most wretched (al-ashaqqayn), though the mention of "its drinking" (suqyaha) does not suit this. ﴿Then they hamstrung her⦆ That is, the most wretched one (al-ashqa). The plural is used, given that he is one person, because all of them were content with his act. Qatadah said: "It has reached us that he did not hamstring her until both their young and old, their males and females, followed him in it." Al-Farra' said: "Two persons hamstrung her, and the Arabs say: 'These two are the best of people.'"

﴿So their Lord brought down upon them⦆ He closed over them the punishment, and it is from the repetition of their saying: "a she-camel mudamdamah," when fat covers her.

﴿for their sin⦆ Because of their sin as described, and the explicit statement of this, together with the indication of it by the particle fa', is for warning about the consequence of sin, so that every sinner may take heed from it.

﴿and He levelled it⦆ That is, the destruction (al-damdamah) among them, so that not one of them escaped, young or old. Or: He levelled Thamud with the ground. Or: He made them equal in destruction.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 91, verse 15:

﴿And He does not fear its consequence.﴾ That is, its outcome and its aftermath, as other rulers who punish fear it, and so they leave off some of the punishment. This is because He, exalted is He, does not do any act except with right, and whoever acts with right does not fear the consequence of his act, even though it is among his nature to fear. The waw is either for the circumstantial state (hal) or for resumption (isti'naf). It has been read "fa-la yakhafu" (so He does not fear), and it has been read "lam yakhaf" (He did not fear).

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-Shams, it is as if he had given in charity everything over which the sun and the moon have risen."
